Coding agents now write code faster than I can read it.
When we give an agent a task, it can quickly implement it.
But if a task is vague, the agent fills the gaps with its own assumptions.
A weak agent that misunderstands us writes fifty lines of broken code.
A strong agent that misunderstands us creates eight files, wires them together, and adds tests that pass.
The code works, but it isn’t what we needed.
We no longer spend most of our time typing.
We spend it saying precisely what we want and checking what came back.
In this article, I show how to make the request specific so the agents don’t need to guess.
